title: How Does a Zip Work?
description: A zip closes in one pull, and it does it with only two parts: two rows of teeth and a slider. This video looks at the problem it solved, what is inside the slider, and why a zip sometimes stops closing.

slides.narration: You close one every day, almost without looking... one pull, and it's done. Before it, boots and dresses were often closed with a long row of small buttons, hooks or laces, fastened one at a time... every morning. The zip turned all of that into a single movement.
slides.image_prompt: a tall old-fashioned boot fastened with a long row of small round buttons up its side, standing alone on a plain wooden table, seen straight on from the side, the whole boot in frame

slides.narration: So how does it work? Each tooth has a small bump on top, and a hollow underneath. The secret is the slider... inside, its channel is shaped like a Y, and it presses the two rows together at an angle, so every bump drops into a hollow on the other side.
slides.image_prompt: a single metal zip lying horizontally across the picture, seen straight on, the only object on a plain background, half open: on the left its two strips of fabric tape spread apart in a wide sideways V, the upper strip angling up and the lower strip angling down, each carrying its own separate row of small metal teeth; in the centre, where the two strips meet, sits the slider; on the right of the slider the two strips run together as one closed strip, their teeth locked into each other

slides.narration: Pull it back, and a wedge inside the slider pries the teeth apart again. And if a zip ever splits open behind the slider... it's often the slider itself, worn loose. That's the whole machine... two rows of teeth, and a slider that tells them when to hold, and when to let go.
slides.image_prompt: Una sola mano baja el cursor de una cremallera medio abierta en la parte delantera de una chaqueta lisa, primer plano, vista de frente: la cremallera tiene un único cursor con un único tirador, y el pulgar y el índice de esa mano pellizcan ese tirador; ningún tirador cuelga del cursor. Por encima del cursor, las dos filas de dientes metálicos se separan.
